tonight.headline: Nothing resolved overnight: McLaurin and Coker are both game-day calls
body: Bad news first, and it's last night's, unchanged. Terry McLaurin, your flex, is still questionable with the hamstring that came up in Friday's practice in London; the only read on it is 'a true game-time decision', and nothing new had been reported by 07:00 this morning. Jalen Coker, his cover, is a game-day call as well: Dave Canales says Carolina will 'move him around again' today 'and then see what it's like on game day'. Justin Jefferson is out. ESPN has it 124.7 to Aye-Aye's 125.0, 50%.

One thing to do, and it's tomorrow at 06:00: check Washington's inactives. If McLaurin is out, Coker goes into the flex; if Coker is then inactive at 16:50, Alvin Kamara, who plays Monday, takes it. Tomorrow's morning brief arrives about half an hour before the 07:30 London lock, so don't wait for it.

case.label: The risk
case.body: McLaurin's 13.1 is still the number most likely to be wrong. He practised in full on Wednesday and Thursday, then the hamstring 'popped up' in Friday's session and he was limited (Pelissero via Yardbarker; Riggo's Rag, 2 Oct). Dan Quinn hasn't spoken about it publicly. A receiver who is active on a day-old hamstring can also play a reduced game, and no inactive list will show that.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Aye-Aye start Herbert (12.6), McCaffrey (20.3), Jeremiyah Love (15.6), Kyren Williams in the flex (13.1), St. Brown (20.2), McMillan (15.0), Tyler Warren (13.1), the Eagles D/ST (6.1) and Aubrey (9.0). None of them carries a game status on NFL.com's list. Aaron Jones (18.1) sits on their bench behind Williams: if they fix that, their number goes up five. Keenan Allen missed Friday's practice for the Colts (ProFootballTalk; RotoWire 2 Oct), which pushes targets toward Warren.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin inactive at 06:00 Sunday: Coker into the flex. Coker inactive at 16:50 Sunday: Kamara into the flex. Both active: the lineup stands as set.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · check inactives Sun 06:00 Mexico City; the flex locks at 07:30 (London)
doFirst.title: If McLaurin is inactive: Coker into the flex, Kamara behind him
doFirst.subtitle: Carried from last night with nothing new: a Friday hamstring, questionable, a game-time decision. Don't move today; the replacement is a game-day call too.

case.label: The injury
case.body: McLaurin practised in full on Wednesday and Thursday, then the hamstring 'popped up' in Friday's practice and he was limited; Washington list him as questionable for the Colts in London (Pelissero via Yardbarker; Riggo's Rag; NFL.com status list, 2 Oct). Yardbarker calls him 'a true game-time decision'. Quinn has said nothing in public and I found nothing dated Saturday by 07:00 Mexico City. It broke after his number was set: ESPN flags him questionable and still projects 13.1. Not priced.

case.label: Why not swap now
case.body: The alternative is Coker at 13.0, a tenth lower, questionable with a quad: a full individual period and limited team snaps on Friday. Canales said on Friday: 'We'd like to push it as far as possible', and that Carolina would 'move him around again tomorrow [Saturday], and then see what it's like on game day' (Panthers Wire via Yahoo, 2 Oct). Swapping one hurt receiver for another on a coin flip isn't an edge, so the projection stands until an inactive list says otherwise.

case.label: The order
case.body: McLaurin's inactives come at 06:00 tomorrow, 90 minutes before the 07:30 kickoff. If he's out, start Coker: he plays Sunday night, so his own inactives arrive at 16:50, and if he's out too Kamara (10.6, Monday 18:15) is still unlocked for the flex. Putting Kamara in first would waste that order.

case.label: Who is throwing
case.body: Marcus Mariota. Jayden Daniels (left elbow) is ruled out (NFL.com status list). Mariota threw McLaurin 9 targets last week for 6 catches, 77 yards and 19.7 points (archive). Coker has Bryce Young, who isn't on Carolina's report.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and the player you put in the flex scores less than the best bench back or receiver left unlocked at the time.

whatWentWrong.title: The flex is a choice between two receivers who are both game-day decisions
whatWentWrong.lead: McLaurin 13.1, questionable (hamstring, Friday). Coker 13.0, questionable (quad, limited all week). Neither changed overnight.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: McLaurin: full Wednesday and Thursday, limited Friday when the hamstring came up (Riggo's Rag 2 Oct). Coker: DNP Wednesday, limited Thursday and Friday; Canales wants to see him move today and decide on game day (Yahoo 2 Oct). With Jefferson out, there's no healthy receiver behind them: the next flex option is a running back.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The card above, and its timing. 06:00 tomorrow is the one check that matters this week, and it comes before tomorrow's brief is any use to you.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Saturday downgrade for either man. This afternoon's run reads it; McLaurin doubtful or out moves Coker in a day early.

whatWentWrong.title: Jefferson's 18.7 sat unpriced through three missed practices
whatWentWrong.lead: The Addison cover was written Wednesday and you fired it on Friday, before the designation. ESPN followed: 18.7 to 0.0, and Addison 11.6 to 14.8.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: DNP Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; ruled out (Vikings.com 2 Oct; NFL.com status list). O'Connell calls him day-to-day and says 'we will not rush Jefferson back before he's at a certain place where we feel like he can go be himself' (carried from Friday).

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Addison starts on the projection, not on an override. It also leaves the flex with no healthy receiver behind it, which is why McLaurin's hamstring is the card above.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. Next Wednesday's practice report decides whether this is one game or several.

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: Cleared for Sunday after two full practices, and he's the man splitting Gordon's work.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Full Thursday and Friday, no designation (NFL.com status list). Hafley: 'should be good to go'. Fowler: the two 'will share the load in the short term' (SI 2 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be your sixth back, splitting a Miami backfield you already own half of, at Minnesota, who allow the 4th-fewest points to RBs (footballdb) and haven't let a back reach 50 rushing yards or score (SI 2 Oct). 3 carries all season (archive). ESPN: 7.5 to Gordon's 9.0.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over outright tomorrow (Gordon under 8 touches): then the Gordon claim is the thing to revisit, not a reason to own both.

doNotChase.name: Kalif Raymond
doNotChase.lead: A free agent since 01:00 this morning, with a backup quarterback expected to throw to him.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 9, 5, 7 targets for 16.4, 9.0 and 21.0 points (archive), the most productive receiver free in this league. The reason is production, not a role change I can name.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 9.8, below McLaurin (13.1), Coker (13.0) and Kamara (10.6), so he doesn't reach your lineup even if both receivers sit. Tyson Bagent is expected to start, his third quarterback in four weeks (Rapoport, NFL.com); the waiver tool didn't surface him because his opportunities fell from Week 1.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin and Coker both ruled out before Sunday's early games, with Jefferson already out: then a healthy receiver is worth Monangai's seat. He's a free agent, so that can wait for the inactive lists.

waiverAnalysis.summary: One question, and it's an artefact: the tool now counts the injured Jefferson as your 'weakest movable' receiver, so Denzel Boston clears him. Three weeks of data, still thin. Nothing clears Monangai at running back.

rising.name: Denzel Boston
rising.roleReason: Cleveland's lead outside receiver: 59 snaps (95%), a route on 92% of dropbacks and 148 air yards, 65% of the team's, on Thursday (RotoWire 2 Oct); 22 targets and 284 yards in four games (CBS 2 Oct). The role is real. The comparison isn't: Jefferson's 3.0 in Week 3 is an ankle injury on his seventh snap.
rising.action: WATCH — on waivers until Wed 01:00, and you dropped him Wednesday for Addison; Tuesday's run compares him with Metcalf for Monangai's seat

settled.title: 'Bowers limited Wednesday and Thursday, not seen Friday' (yesterday's briefs)
settled.result: Raiders.com's final report has it the other way: no practice Wednesday or Thursday, limited Friday, no game status. It touches the Tre Tucker watch, not your lineup.

settled.title: 'Wright limited Thursday' (Thursday afternoon's brief)
settled.result: He was upgraded to a full practice (FantasyPros, NBC, RotoWire, CBS, 1 Oct). The brief went out about an hour after the report. Gordon's row is corrected: it's a split.

settled.title: Coker in the flex over McLaurin (21 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Coker 3.8, McLaurin 19.7 on the bench. Closed WRONG. It was also a coin flip that should never have had a thesis.

settled.title: Hold Likely through the Giants' quarterback change (22 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: 3.3 on 5 targets, so the under-six clause fired. Closed WRONG, not EXPIRED.

settled.title: Hold Pineiro over McPherson (23 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Pineiro 8, McPherson 11. The written falsifier didn't fire, so it stays open, but the hold lost 3 points.

settled.title: Start Warren over Tuten (13 Sep, reviewed weekly)
settled.result: Archive: 20.6 to 17.0 in Week 3; 2 of 3 weeks won. Closed RIGHT.

settled.title: Let Kyle Pitts go; Chem can't use a second TE (23 Sep)
Decline Jaxson Dart at 83% owned (23 Sep)
settled.result: Out for the season with knee damage (Bleacher Report, 28 Sep). Closed RIGHT.

cannotSee.label: McLaurin's hamstring
cannotSee.body: A Friday addition with no severity reported and no word from Quinn. Nothing dated Saturday existed at 07:00. The inactive list at 06:00 Sunday says whether he dresses; it can't say whether he plays a full game.

cannotSee.label: Coker's quad
cannotSee.body: Canales wanted to see him move today and decide on game day. Whatever Carolina saw this morning isn't reported yet; this afternoon's run reads it.

cannotSee.label: Reports I couldn't retrieve
cannotSee.body: Hogs Haven's Washington table (blocked), ESPN's inactives column (it returned an empty page), NBC's usage report and RotoBaller's Tre Tucker note (navigation only). A CBS note on the Dolphins' backs turned out to be from December 2025 and an SI piece on Wan'Dale Robinson from August; both were discarded.

cannotSee.label: Chicago's quarterback
cannotSee.body: Not announced. Rapoport expects Bagent; Ben Johnson says Sunday. It touches Monangai, who is benched, and Raymond, who is a do-not-chase.

cannotSee.label: Matchup sample
cannotSee.body: footballdb's tables are standard scoring through Week 3; it has no PPR table. Allen's tile predates New England ruling out Gonzalez and Barmore. Pineiro's tile rests on three games of kicker points.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Raymond is a free agent as of this morning; Metcalf, Dowdle and Boston clear on Wed 7 Oct at 01:00.

cannotSee.label: The wire screen
cannotSee.body: wire_screen.py counts Week 4 as a stat week once one game is played, so its list is Steelers and Browns plus Tyler Higbee. Same eleven names as yesterday and no newcomers, so the verdicts are carried. It can't see Holani, Lemon or Raymond; they're in do-not-chase from the ownership column instead.

cannotSee.label: Atlanta and Las Vegas
cannotSee.body: Kyle Pitts isn't on Atlanta's Friday report and drew an 8% target share in Week 3 (FantasyPros 1 Oct); his snap share, which the decision log's test uses, I still don't have. For Tre Tucker I have Bowers' practice line and nothing on Tucker himself.
